chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Muhammadi narrated to us from his book in the year sixty-eight and two hundred, saying: Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqal narrated to us, from his father, saying: I entered upon Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) and there was a group with him.

While we were conversing and he was facing one of his companions, he turned to us and said: 'In what matter are you? Far, far! That which you eagerly await will not come until you are tested (purified). Far! That which you eagerly await will not come until you are distinguished (clarified). That which you eagerly await will not come until you are sifted (separated from impurities). That which you eagerly await will not come except after despair. That which you eagerly await will not come until the wretched one becomes wretched and the happy one becomes happy.'

key_terms.إِيَاسٌ: Despair (giving up hope of immediate relief)
key_terms.تَغْرَبَلُوا: You are sifted (separated from impurities like sifting flour)
key_terms.تُمَيَّزُوا: You are distinguished/clarified (separated from the weak)
key_terms.تُمْحَصُوا: You are tested/purified (like gold being purified)
key_terms.وَيَسْعَدَ مَنْ سَعَدَ: And the happy one becomes happy

ai.seo_question: What conditions must be met before the awaited relief comes for the Shia according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) outlines the spiritual purification process required of the Shia during the Minor and Major Disappearance, using metaphors of 'testing' (imḥāṣ), 'distinguishing' (tamayyuz), and 'sifting' (gharbala) to separate the sincere from the hypocritical. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view that the delay in the Imam's reappearance is not an absence but a period of rigorous spiritual refinement, ensuring that only those destined for success (saʿada) or ruin (shaqāwa) are fully prepared for the final establishment of divine justice.
